points.label: Action and response
points.left: David seeks a survivor of Saul’s house for Jonathan’s sake, restores Saul’s land to Mephibosheth, seats him at the royal table, and appoints Ziba’s household to work the land.
points.right: David sends comfort to Hanun, messengers are humiliated, Ammon hires Syria, Joab divides the army, and repeated battles end in Syrian submission.

points.label: Evidence boundary
points.left: The source places covenant loyalty changes Mephibosheth’s place and provision inside this David setting without explaining every motive, transition, or later consequence.
points.right: The source places a condolence becomes international war through another court’s interpretation inside this David setting without explaining every motive, transition, or later consequence.

payload.posture: 2 Samuel 9:1–13 and 2 Samuel 10:1–19 are distinct approved David Scenes in the authored “Ark, House, and Kingdom” movement; holding them together exposes what continues and what changes without collapsing their sources.
payload.tension: 2 Samuel 9:1–13 foregrounds covenant loyalty changes Mephibosheth’s place and provision; 2 Samuel 10:1–19 foregrounds a condolence becomes international war through another court’s interpretation. Their sequence does not by itself explain every change between them.
payload.title: Power remembers Jonathan’s covenant / Kindness is interpreted as espionage
